title: THE MAN WITH THE WRONG KEY

suspects.name: Unidentified Meeting Contact
suspects.description: A person the fictional route of objects and stops points toward, never directly identified.

suspects.name: Rental Counter Clerk
suspects.description: Issued the Nissan rental with the mismatched key.

related_persons.name: Motel Desk Clerk
related_persons.description: Checked Blair into the Knoxville-area motel room where he was later found.

related_persons.name: Border Crossing Agent
related_persons.description: Logged Blair's crossing from Canada into the United States.

timeline.event: Blair crosses from Canada into the United States carrying multiple currencies and valuables
Blair rents a Nissan; the key issued does not match the vehicle he is later found with
Blair follows a route through several unplanned-looking stops with maps and travel notes
Blair checks into a motel room near Knoxville
A forty-minute gap in the room before Blair is found dead

evidence.name: The Wrong Key
evidence.description: A Nissan key found on Blair's person that does not open any vehicle on record as belonging to him.

evidence.name: Cross-Border Travel Log
evidence.description: Confirms Blair's route and timing across the Canada–US border.

evidence.name: Currency and Valuables Inventory
evidence.description: Blair was carrying multiple currencies and valuable items, nearly all of which remained on his person at death.

evidence.name: Motel Check-In Record
evidence.description: Check-in time and room assignment; establishes the window before Blair was found.

evidence.name: Forty-Minute Room Gap
evidence.description: No confirmed account of what occurred in the room during the forty minutes before Blair was found.

evidence.name: Maps and Travel Notes
evidence.description: Annotated maps and handwritten notes found among Blair's belongings, forming a pattern of stops that does not obviously resemble tourism.

puzzles.name: The Wrong Key
puzzles.description: Identify why the mismatched key matters rather than dismissing it as confusion.

puzzles.name: The Route
puzzles.description: Map the sequence of destinations against the maps and notes, and examine why multiple currencies and valuables were being carried together.

puzzles.name: The Hotel Room
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the forty-minute sequence inside the motel room using check-in timing and scene evidence.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Labels the gap as an ordinary delay (unpacking, resting) and downplays its significance unless directly challenged.

puzzles.name: The Meeting Hypothesis
puzzles.description: Identify what evidence supports or contradicts the idea that Blair's stops were a planned route toward a meeting, and what the investigation cannot establish about who he intended to meet.

puzzles.name: Final Reconstruction
puzzles.description: Distinguish a genuine coordinated pattern from coincidental randomness in Blair's itinerary.

hypotheses.statement: Blair was simply disoriented and the anomalies (wrong key, unusual route) reflect confusion, not planning.
Blair's itinerary was a deliberate route made of objects, locations, and instructions, built around an intended meeting.
Blair's death was the result of a simple robbery.
Blair was following a plan whose other participant never appears directly in the evidence.
